transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hello. Um... well, I guess I'm just having some trouble keeping up at work lately. 

I'll start working on an EPIC quality report, or I'll sit down in a clinic metrics meeting, and... I don't know. Within a few minutes, my mind just drifts. I end up rereading the same numbers over and over, or I realize I completely missed the point of the discussion. So... I figured I should probably come in.
Did you have this same kind of trouble paying attention when you were a child?

I suppose so, yes. Um... even back in elementary school. I remember teachers writing on my report cards that I was bright, but... careless. And my mother pretty much had to sit with me while I finished my homework. Otherwise, I'd just... lose track of the assignments, or realize I forgot my books at school.
Do you also have this same kind of trouble staying focused in everyday tasks at home?
Um... I'm not really sure. I guess I haven't paid much attention to how I am at home. It's mostly just... work where I really notice it.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about different things, even when you try not to?
No, not really. I mean... I have normal stress, I suppose, but I wouldn't say I worry about things constantly.
Outside of work, do you also have trouble staying focused during everyday tasks at home?
I... I think you just asked me that. Like I said, I haven't really noticed. It's just work where it's a problem.
Have you been feeling down or depressed مؤخراً?
No. Um... I don't think so. I mean, I wouldn't say I'm depressed. Just... fine, I guess.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?
No. Um... I sleep fine. It hasn't really been an issue.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview supports a longstanding attention/concentration disorder with onset in childhood and current impairment at work. The patient reports distractibility, difficulty sustaining attention in meetings and report review, repeated rereading, and childhood history of careless school performance, needing supervision for homework, losing track of assignments, and forgetting books. Anxiety, depression, and sleep disturbance were not supported as better explanations in the interview. Although cross-situational adult symptoms were not clearly established, the provided differential set contains only F98.8, which best fits the presentation.
